inline_comments.comment: The priority order in this array contradicts the documented intent. `getMostCriticalStatusValue` iterates `statusPriority` left-to-right and keeps the last match, so a higher index means more critical. The current placement makes `new` (index 5) the most critical of the three new values, then `modified` (index 4), then `affected` (index 3) — i.e. `new > modified > affected`. But the PR description explicitly states `affected > modified > new`, the `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority` story comment repeats the same order, and the test name 'should rank affected above modified and below warning' also implies `affected` is most critical. To match the stated intent, the order should be reversed: `['status-value:new', 'status-value:modified', 'status-value:affected', 'status-value:warning', 'status-value:error']`.

The test description contradicts the assertion. The name 'should rank affected above modified and below warning' implies `affected` is more critical than `modified`, but the first `expect` call passes `['status-value:affected', 'status-value:modified', 'status-value:success']` and asserts `'status-value:modified'` wins — proving `modified > affected`, which is the opposite of the name. Either the assertion is wrong (should return `'status-value:affected'` to match the name and the PR's documented intent) or the name is wrong. As-is, the test name actively misleads about which value has higher priority.

`StatusIconMap` is used to populate the context-menu `statusLinks` (the icon next to each status entry in the right-click menu). Returning `null` for `'status-value:new'`, `'status-value:modified'`, and `'status-value:affected'` means these statuses will appear without icons in the context menu, while every other status value has one. The SVG icons are already defined in `status.tsx` via `getStatus()` — consider referencing those same icons here (e.g. `getStatus(theme, 'status-value:new')[0]`) or adding dedicated `ReactNode` constants so the context menu entries are consistent.

`getStatus` returns `null` as the color for `'status-value:new'`, `'status-value:modified'`, and `'status-value:affected'`, while `StatusButton.tsx` independently maps those same values to `theme.fgColor.accent`. The two sources of color truth are now out of sync — `getStatus`'s color is used for branch-label text coloring in `Tree.tsx` (`const color = status ? getStatus(theme, status)[1] : null`), so those branch labels will not be recoloured for the three new statuses even though the icon button is. If the accent colour should also apply to the label, change `null` to `theme.fgColor.accent` here. If the difference is intentional, add a comment explaining why.

The comment in `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority` states `'most critical wins: error > warning > affected > modified > new'`, but the current `statusPriority` array makes `new` the most critical of the three (`new > modified > affected`). The comment will mislead anyone reading this story or the test output. Once the priority array bug is resolved this comment should be updated to match the final intended order.

`StatusesChangeDetectionPriority` is described as being there 'to verify priority ordering', but its `play` function (`waitForChecklistWidget`) makes no assertions about which icon or colour is actually rendered. Without any DOM assertions, this story cannot catch a future regression in priority logic. Consider adding assertions such as checking that the group-level status icon shown is the expected highest-priority variant, e.g.:
```ts
await canvas.findByRole('button', { name: 'Status: error' });
```

general_comments.comment: There is a systemic inconsistency in the PR between intent and implementation for the priority ordering of the three new status values. The PR description, the story comment in `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority`, and the test name 'should rank affected above modified and below warning' all describe the intended order as `affected > modified > new` (affected being the most urgent, as it signals a possible silent regression in a story that wasn't directly touched). However, `statusPriority` in `status.tsx` is ordered `[…, 'affected', 'modified', 'new', …]`, making `new` the most critical of the three because `getMostCriticalStatusValue` returns the entry with the highest index. This affects every consumer of `getMostCriticalStatusValue`, `getGroupStatus`, and `showBranchStatus`. The fix is to swap the order to `[…, 'new', 'modified', 'affected', …]` and update the test assertions accordingly.

The five new Sidebar stories (`StatusesNew`, `StatusesModified`, `StatusesAffected`, `StatusesMixed`, `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority`) all use `play: waitForChecklistWidget` without any assertions specific to the new status indicators. Since this PR's core value is the new icon/colour rendering, at minimum the stories should assert that the correct `aria-label` (e.g. `'Status: new'`) appears on status buttons, or that the correct icon element is present. As-is, the stories are purely visual and would not catch a regression where the icons silently disappear.
